title: IoT Hub Message Routing vs Event Grid — Why Telemetry and Events Are Not the Same Problem
description:
Machine telemetry and device events both arrive through Azure IoT Hub, but treating them as the same thing either floods workflows with sensor noise or buries urgent signals in a pipeline nobody watches. This episode is for IoT, OT and Azure architects building manufacturing data platforms. You will learn when to use IoT Hub message routing, when to use Event Grid, and how MES and asset context turn signals into trustworthy production decisions.
In this episode
00:00 – A press line, a sensor stream and one missing signal05:30 – Telemetry versus discrete events22:10 – What Azure IoT Hub actually handles27:30 – IoT Hub message routing as the telemetry data plane44:50 – Azure Event Grid, IoT Hub events and the connection state trap66:40 – Lifecycle events, filtering and ERP, MES and asset context83:30 – Gateway offline during a work order and the two wrong designs100:40 – Data plane, control plane, Fabric and Power BI
Key takeaways
Telemetry is a time-ordered production record that needs sequence, retention and independent readers, while a discrete event is a notice that something changed and someone may need to react.IoT Hub message routing is the telemetry data plane into Event Hubs, storage and Microsoft Fabric, whereas Event Grid is a notification fabric with at-least-once, unordered delivery that handlers must treat as a prompt to check current state.A device disconnect only proves lost cloud visibility, so production conclusions need MES, ERP and asset model context, shared device identity and explicit data contracts across both paths.
